question.text: This northern neighbor of Germany lies on the Jutland peninsula. It also controls Greenland.
question.clue: This country was defeated in one war after its adversary marched over a frozen strait to surprise its forces.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of Scandinavian countries.
swap.text: This country was led by the "Lion from the North" Gustavus Adolphus during the Thirty Years' War. This former kingdom fought the Great Northern War against Russia under Charles XII.
swap.clue: In this home country of Ellen Key, 30,000 farmers supported the funding of the "F-ship" by marching to its Royal Palace Yard, kicking off the "Courtyard Crisis."

question.leadin: This member of the House of Vasa defeated Count Tilly in his most famous victory, Breitenfeld.
question.text: Name this man who died at the Battle of Lutzen and was known as the "Lion of the North."
question.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav Adolf; Gustav II; Gustavus the Great; prompt on “Gustav” or “Gustavus”]
question.clue: At the Battle of Lech, also known as the "Battle of Rain," he commanded troops over the Count of Tilly.

swap.text: The goal of Scott's expedition was to be the first men to reach the South Pole. When they arrived, however, they were devastated to learn that a crew led by this Norwegian had beaten them to it by four weeks.
swap.clue: This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott's by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.

question.leadin: Before one battle in this war, the losing side's king was incapacitated by a leg injury received while personally scouting enemy redoubts.
question.text: Name this war during which Charles XII was defeated at the Battle of Poltava. This war ended with Peter the Great forcing Sweden to sign the Treaty of Nystad.
question.answerHtml: Great Northern War [or Second Northern War; prompt on Northern War]
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.leadin: The Mannerheim Line was a defensive fortification during this conflict in which "Molotov cocktails" were first used.
swap.text: Name this 1939-1940 "seasonal" conflict during which the Soviet Union attempted to invade Finland.
swap.clue: The invading side was expelled from the League of Nations as a result, and a major goal of the war was to cut off Germany's supply of iron ore.

question.leadin: In May of 1940, this nation was invaded by Great Britain in Operation Fork.
question.text: Name this island nation with capital at Reykjavik, whose Althing voted to remain neutral during World War II.
question.clue: Local lords called godr in this region met at the Law Rock, over which the Lawspeaker presided.

swap.leadin: This country saw a civil war that pitted the White Guard against the Red Guard.
swap.text: Name this northern European country once home to the radical Lapua Movement. It hosted the 1952 Olympics in its capital of Helsinki.
swap.clue: As a grand duchy, this country's capital was originally at Turku.

question.leadin: Identify these victims of brazen assassinations from European history.
question.text: South Africa's most evil export, superspy Craig Williamson, may have been responsible for the 1986 shooting of this Swedish Prime Minister, an ardent opponent of Apartheid.
question.clue: This man claimed that apartheid "cannot be reformed, it has to be eliminated", which Eugene de Kock later testified may have led to his death.

swap.text: The majority of prisoners rescued in the "White Buses" campaign were originally from this country, where Josef Terboven was installed as military governor during its Nazi occupation.
swap.clue: Another leader of this country served with Josef Terboven and was executed with Albert Hagelin after establishing a fascist government.

question.leadin: This leader was killed at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, ending his claim to the English throne.
question.text: Name this warrior who ruled Norway from 1046 to 1066. This king's Norse epithet is often translated as "severe" or "tough ruler."
question.answerHtml: Harald Hardrada [or Harald III or Harald Sigurdsson; prompt on Harald or Hardrada]
question.clue: This man married the daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, Elisiv of Kiev, on his return from Constantinople.

swap.text: To the west of Finland is this gulf and northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It contains the Aland Islands and serves to separate Finland and Sweden.
swap.clue: The Aland [Oh-land]Islands, a Swedish-speaking archipelago forming an autonomous region of Finland, are found in this gulf, the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. This gulf separates Finland and Sweden.

question.leadin: Construction on this fortification began after the signing of the Treaty of Tartu in 1920, which established a border between two countries on the Karelian Isthmus.
question.text: Name this defensive fortification constructed between Taipale and the Gulf of Finland.
question.clue: Reinforced concrete and protection plates were dropped from this due to a rise in the price of steel, and parts of it were simply strategically placed mounds of soil known as "slope cuts."

swap.text: Due to skepticism over Henson's voyage, the first undisputed expedition to the North Pole was led by this Norwegian explorer, the first to reach the South Pole and traverse the Northwest Passage.
swap.clue: This person led the crew that disappeared searching for the airship Italia and was the first to successfully navigate the North-west Passage in a boat, the Gjoa .

question.text: While king, Harald assassinated Einar Thambalskelfir, who had supported Magnus and led opposition to this half-brother of Harald's. This saint and King of Norway died fighting a peasant army at Stiklestad.

swap.leadin: This man became the highest-profile person to be executed in a "legal purge" in his country after World War II.
swap.text: Name this politician who overthrew Haakon VII to take power in 1940.
swap.clue: This man was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire for his humanitarian works, which included a stint in the Ukraine trying to help alleviate a famine there in 1921 undertaken at the behest of mountain climbing-humanitarian Fridtjof Nansen.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the incestuous mixing of Scandinavian nations.
question.text: At this 1814 convention, which followed the Treaty of Kiel, the defeated Norway was forced into a personal union with Sweden ruled jointly by Swedish king Charles XIII, which lasted until 1905.

swap.leadin: A drum used by these people can be found in the rock carvings at Alta.
swap.text: Identify this culture of reindeer herding Europeans who live near the Arctic Circle. They construct tents called lavvu and speak an Uralic language.
swap.answerHtml: Sami People [or Saami People or Same People or Lapp People (although this last name is not in polite use anymore)]
swap.clue: Protests against the construction of the Alta hydroelectric power station strengthened activism for these people's rights and led to the 1989 formation of their first parliament.

question.text: The Finnish-German alliance did not stay intact, and in this 1944-45 war, Germany decided to secure Petsamo while their 20th Mountain Army got consistently owned in the namesake geographical region.
question.clue: After signing an armistice with the Soviet Union in 1944, Finland fought this war in order to expel German troops from its territory.

swap.text: The Norwegian language debate erupted after Norwegian elites began favoring an independent language during Norway's union with Sweden under this royal family, established by a Napoleonic general who took the regnal name Charles XIV.
swap.clue: The founder of this dynasty was once implicated in the Rennes Plot, and became the governor of Hanover and Bremen before being awarded the title of Prince of Pontecorvo.
